drills.title: Fast Fibonacci with a local loop
hints: Define `fibFast`, taking n : Nat and returning a Nat.
Inside it, declare a local recursive helper `loop : Nat → Nat × Nat`, defined by equations on its argument.
At 0, loop returns the pair (0, 1).
At n+1, locally bind p to loop n, then return the pair of p's second component and the sum of p's first and second components.
The result of fibFast is the second component of loop n.

drills.title: Replicate with an accumulator loop
hints: Define `replicate`, taking n : Nat and a : α (α left auto-bound), returning a List α.
Inside it, declare a local recursive helper `loop : Nat → List α → List α`, defined by equations on both arguments, naming the accumulator `as`.
At 0, return the accumulator unchanged.
At n+1, recurse on n with a consed onto the front of the accumulator.
The body of replicate runs loop from n with the empty list.
Check the type of the generated auxiliary `replicate.loop`, with all its arguments made explicit.

drills.title: Well-founded recursion via WellFounded.fix
hints: Define a noncomputable function `f`, with an implicit type α : Sort u.

Its explicit parameters: a relation r : α → α → Prop, a proof h that r is well-founded, a motive C : α → Sort v, and a recipe F which, for each x : α, given a function producing C y for every y with r y x, produces C x.
Its result type is the dependent function type assigning to each x : α an element of C x.
Its body is WellFounded.fix applied to h and F.

drills.title: Unfolding div on the left-hand side
hints: Anonymous example: for x y : Nat, div x y equals (if 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x then div (x - y) y + 1 else 0). Prove it in tactic mode.
Enter conversion mode, move to the left-hand side, and unfold div there only.
Close the goal with rfl.
Second anonymous example: for x y : Nat and h : 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x, prove div x y = div (x - y) y + 1 in tactic mode.
As before, unfold div on the left-hand side only, in conversion mode.
Finish with simp, using h.

drills.title: Ackermann with lexicographic termination
hints: Define `ack : Nat → Nat → Nat` by equations on both arguments.
ack 0 y is y+1.
ack (x+1) 0 is ack x 1.
ack (x+1) (y+1) is ack x applied to ack (x+1) y.
Justify termination by mapping the arguments x and y to the pair (x, y).

drills.title: Division with a custom decreasing proof
hints: Theorem `div_lemma`: for implicit x y : Nat, 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x → x - y < x, in term mode.
Prove it by a lambda that destructures the conjunction into `ypos` and `ylex`.
The body applies Nat.sub_lt to (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le ypos ylex) and to ypos.
Define `div (x y : Nat) : Nat`: if 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x (naming that proof h), return div (x - y) y + 1; otherwise 0.
Supply your own proof that the recursive call decreases: apply div_lemma, then close what remains with assumption.

drills.title: Ackermann with explicit termination proofs
hints: Define `ack : Nat → Nat → Nat` by equations on both arguments: ack 0 y is y+1; ack (x+1) 0 is ack x 1; ack (x+1) (y+1) is ack x (ack (x+1) y).
Justify termination by mapping the arguments x and y to the pair (x, y).
Supply the decreasing proofs yourself: first run simp_wf on all goals at once.
Then take the three goals in turn as focused bullets. First: apply Prod.Lex.left, then simp with arithmetic enabled.
Second: apply Prod.Lex.right, then simp with arithmetic enabled.
Third: same as the first.

drills.title: Ackermann is always positive
hints: Theorem `ack_gt_zero`: ack n m > 0 (n and m left auto-bound), in tactic mode.
Do functional induction following ack, and on every resulting goal run simp with all hypotheses in context plus ack's defining equations.

drills.title: Five-way or by function cases
hints: Theorem `f_or`: f b1 b2 b3 b4 b5 equals the boolean or of b1, b2, b3, b4, b5 (the b's left auto-bound), in tactic mode.
Split into cases following the branches of f, using fun_cases, and close every resulting goal with simp_all.

drills.title: Inverting the mutual Even/Odd predicates
hints: Open the namespaces Even and Odd.
Theorem `not_odd_zero`: ¬ Odd 0. Prove it by a lambda over h that eliminates h with an empty match.
Theorem `even_of_odd_succ`: ∀ n, Odd (n + 1) → Even n, defined by equations directly on its arguments.
Its only case ignores the number, matches the proof as odd_succ n h, and returns h.
Theorem `odd_of_even_succ`: ∀ n, Even (n + 1) → Odd n, in the same way, its only case matching even_succ n h.

drills.title: Inverting a function on its image
hints: Declare an inductive family `ImageOf`, with implicit α β : Type u and parameter f : α → β, indexed by β and living in Type u.
Its one constructor `imf` takes a : α and produces ImageOf f (f a).
Open the ImageOf namespace.
Define `inverse`, with implicit f : α → β, of type (b : β) → ImageOf f b → α, by equations.
Its single case: the first argument is f a, marked as inaccessible; the second is imf a; return a.
Define `inverse'` the same way, except that the first argument is just a wildcard.

drills.title: Pointwise addition of vectors
hints: Define `add`, requiring an Add α instance, of type: for implicit n : Nat, Vect α n → Vect α n → Vect α n, by equations.
In both cases, match the implicit length too, but as an inaccessible wildcard.
Two nils give nil.
cons a as and cons b bs give cons of a + b onto add of as and bs.

drills.title: Division via WellFounded.fix
hints: Open the Nat namespace.
Theorem `div_lemma`: for implicit x y : Nat, 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x → x - y < x, in term mode.
Prove it by a lambda over h: apply sub_lt to Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le of h's left and right components, and to h's left component.
Define `div.F`, taking x : Nat, then f : a dependent function from x₁ : Nat and a proof that x₁ < x to Nat → Nat, then y : Nat, and returning a Nat.
If 0 < y ∧ y ≤ x holds, with its proof named h, return f applied to x - y, div_lemma h and y, plus 1.
Otherwise return zero (unqualified, thanks to the opened namespace).
Define `div`, marked noncomputable, as WellFounded.fix applied to the well-foundedness field of measure id and to div.F.
